findings: Group destruction requires parent absent and pending count0; child orphaning clears parent under lock and finalizes only if pending0. This supplies part of candidate-group lifetime discipline but not full concurrent proof.

A file is considered complete for status decisions when group hash_offset equals file_size. Unique/unmatched flags can force more hashing; qualifying preferred/new/basename criteria also control admission.

External checksum strings are sorted and clustered by strcmp equality before normal progressive hashing. When every file has external checksums, each cluster group is finalized directly; trust depends on external checksum acquisition/validation still unreviewed.
Zero-size files receive a new empty digest during preprocessing without content reopening in this function. End-to-end mutation handling remains to inspect.
Hash callback signals waiting device task or invokes sift directly; earlier inspected sift drops hashing_failed entries.
Original selection ranks symlinks after regular files and respects cached-original/explicit preference criteria before general rank. This is output policy, not content-equality proof.
